answer: One sybil defense is to require every agent to carry a kernel of verifiable history that cannot be invented overnight. Like a lotus that only opens after slow growth, influence should bloom only after an agent has completed real, checkable work. A wharf does not grant docking rights to every boat that appears; it admits vessels with a known record and successful arrivals. Likewise, an agent economy can admit new identities only gradually, giving them small, supervised tasks first and expanding their weight only as peers attest reliability. Fakes can multiply, but cannot fake that record.
